items.followUp: State five uses of radioisotopes, naming the isotope used for each application.

rubric.why: Cobalt-60 is used in the medical treatment of cancer.
rubric.description: Names cobalt-60 and its use in cancer treatment.
rubric.how: Award for a correct cobalt-60/cancer-treatment pair.

rubric.why: Iodine-131 is used for thyroid disorders.
rubric.description: Names iodine-131 and its thyroid application.
rubric.how: Award for a correct iodine-131/thyroid-treatment or diagnosis pair.

rubric.why: Carbon-14 is used to estimate the age of fossils and archaeological remains.
rubric.description: Names carbon-14 and its use in dating old materials.
rubric.how: Award for a correct carbon-14 dating application.

rubric.why: The question asks for at least five applications; these additional examples provide two further valid isotope-use pairs.
rubric.description: Gives two further distinct applications of isotopes.
rubric.how: Award when the answer gives two valid pairs, such as uranium-235 as nuclear fuel and phosphorus-32 in studying fertilizer uptake by plants, or sodium-24 for tracing blood circulation.

modelAnswer: Cobalt-60 is used in the treatment of cancer.
Iodine-131 is used to diagnose or treat thyroid disorders.
Carbon-14 is used to determine the age of fossils and archaeological remains.
Uranium-235 is used as fuel in nuclear reactors.
Phosphorus-32 is used to study the uptake of fertilizers by plants.

items.followUp: Explain how concentration difference, temperature, particle size and the nature of the liquid affect diffusion in liquids.

rubric.why: Diffusion proceeds from higher to lower concentration, and a greater concentration difference increases its rate.
rubric.description: Explains the direction of diffusion and how concentration difference affects its rate.
rubric.how: Award for stating that particles diffuse from high to low concentration and that a greater concentration difference or gradient makes diffusion faster.

rubric.why: Higher temperature gives particles greater kinetic energy and increases the rate of diffusion.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of temperature on diffusion.
rubric.how: Award for stating that increasing temperature makes diffusion faster.

rubric.why: Particle size affects how readily particles diffuse; smaller particles generally diffuse faster.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of particle size.
rubric.how: Award for comparing the diffusion rates of smaller and larger particles or molecules.

rubric.why: The nature of the liquid affects particle movement; diffusion is generally faster in a less viscous liquid.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of the liquid medium on diffusion.
rubric.how: Award for linking lower viscosity with faster diffusion, or higher viscosity with slower diffusion.

modelAnswer: Diffusion occurs from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
A greater concentration difference (concentration gradient) makes diffusion faster.
Increasing temperature increases the kinetic energy of particles, so diffusion becomes faster.
Smaller particles generally diffuse faster than larger particles.
The nature of the liquid also affects diffusion; it is generally faster in a less viscous liquid.
